facts.text: The resort is set in the Umbrian countryside near Perugia.
facts.excerpt: Nestled in the verdant Umbrian countryside near Perugia, Italy, Borgo dei Conti Resort is a luxurious country retreat that marries noble medieval origins with modern hospitality.

facts.text: The resort was restored by the Spagnulo & Partners architectural studio, integrating local craftsmanship and Renaissance art elements.
facts.excerpt: owing to its meticulous restoration by the Spagnulo & Partners Architectural Studio. This restoration has successfully integrated local craftsmanship and Renaissance art elements

facts.text: Rooms feature period frescoes, coffered ceilings and views of the countryside or the resort's cloister.
facts.excerpt: Guests can expect period frescoes, coffered ceilings, and breathtaking views of the countryside or the resort's cloister

facts.text: Room types include the Rossi Scotti Apartments, the Conti Suite and the Conte Suite.
facts.excerpt: Each room, including the Rossi Scotti Apartments, Conti Suite, Conte Suite, and more, offers its unique charm and contemporary luxury.

facts.text: Dining includes fine dining at Cedri Restaurant, casual meals at Osteria del Borgo and drinks at the Lounge Bar.
facts.excerpt: from the fine dining experience at Cedri Restaurant to casual meals at Osteria del Borgo, and a variety of drinks at the Lounge Bar

facts.text: Activities include outdoor cinema, picnics in the olive grove, cooking classes, wine tasting and truffle hunting.
facts.excerpt: the resort offers numerous activities such as outdoor cinema, romantic dinners, picnics in the olive grove, cooking classes, wine tasting, and truffle hunting

facts.text: The spa is in the villa's western wing and offers indoor and outdoor wellness experiences.
facts.excerpt: the luxurious spa in the villa's western wing provides both indoor and outdoor wellness experiences

facts.text: The area around the resort has Etruscan remnants, medieval villages and hamlets.
facts.excerpt: Surrounded by Etruscan remnants, medieval villages, and charming hamlets, guests have numerous opportunities for cultural and outdoor pursuits.

facts.text: The resort has an outdoor infinity pool and forest walking trails.
facts.excerpt: In the summer heat, the capacious outdoor infinity pool comes into its own, but the resort’s forest walking trails, two restaurants, and a spa that seems to go on forever

facts.text: The resort has a seasonal opening from April to November.
facts.excerpt: make it a perfect long weekend destination even at the cooler extremes of its April to November seasonal opening

facts.text: Artist-aristocrat Lemmo Rossi Scotti, Count of Montepetriolo, transformed the property into a Gothic Revival castle-villa surrounded by an English-style park.
facts.excerpt: transformed the property into a grand Gothic Revival castle-villa surrounded by an English-style park

facts.text: The Conte and Contessa piano nobile suites have original frescoed friezes and ornate heraldic fireplaces.
facts.excerpt: two “piano nobile” suites, Conte and Contessa, that are full of original detail from the era of the Rossi Scotti counts, such as frescoed friezes and ornate heraldic fireplaces

facts.text: The entrance is a fortified gate, with a winding road up through an ilex forest to the estate buildings.
facts.excerpt: leads you up a winding road through a dark ilex forest to the sunny heights above

facts.text: Perugia is less than half an hour away by car.
facts.excerpt: Perugia, with its art, shopping, and summer Umbria Jazz festival, is less than half an hour away by car.

facts.text: Pets are welcome; five terrace suites are advised for dog owners.
facts.excerpt: Pets are welcome; dog owners are advised to book one of five terrace suites

facts.text: Rooms all have roomy double-sink bathrooms.
facts.excerpt: a series of spacious rooms, all different, all with roomy double-sink bathrooms
